name: Voice Hold
description:
Hold a key and speak. Offline dictation, text arrives as you talk.

Hold the shortcut (Ctrl+Space by default), speak, release: the words are typed in the text field under your cursor while you talk, block by block, with a grey live preview. A quick tap keeps listening hands-free (tap again, Escape or a few seconds of silence stop it). A small pill slides out of the top bar while you dictate, with the microphone level and the live text, and goes back into it when you stop.

Everything runs on your computer, offline: French, English and 23 other European languages are recognised with punctuation (Parakeet TDT 0.6B Ultra through sherpa-onnx). No account, no network, no cloud.

Optional voice commands, off by default: a second shortcut (Ctrl+Alt+Space), say what to do. Opening an application, the volume, dark mode or a workspace happen at once; a shell command is shown first and only runs after you confirm. What the rules do not know goes to a small language model that the engine runs on your computer (llama.cpp, a separate download of about 1.3 GB). The same model can polish dictated blocks; that is off by default too.

The speech engine is a separate download (Python, GPL, about 500 MB with its models) that cannot be part of this package; nothing works without it. The extension installs it for you: a notification and the settings open an Installation page with one Install button, no terminal and no password, and a field to try the dictation in. Requires PipeWire and Python 3.12 or newer. Wayland only; applications must use the GNOME input method (GTK, Qt, Electron with Wayland; terminals get the text without the preview).

What the extension does outside the shell, stated plainly:
- Network: only after you click Install in the preferences (Installation page, or the Commands page for the language model). The extension itself, while you dictate, never touches the network. The Installation page then reads a list of files pinned to a tagged release (raw.githubusercontent.com/d101c/hold-setup, tag v0.6) and downloads the engine and the speech models; every file is checked against the SHA-256 of that list before it is unpacked.
- Files written: the engine and its packages in ~/.local/share/hold, the models in ~/.local/share/voice-hold, and the D-Bus service file ~/.local/share/dbus-1/services/org.griffit.VoiceHold.service (the voice commands add org.griffit.VoiceHold.Commands.service, and the language model goes in ~/.local/share/voice-hold/llm). Nothing is written outside your home folder, and no administrator right is used.
- Subprocess: from the preferences only, on a click on the Commands page Install button, the installed engine is run once as `setup --commands` to download the language model. The shell process itself starts nothing but the D-Bus activation of the engine and, for a voice command you confirmed, what the engine runs in a visible terminal.
- Clipboard: the Copy buttons in the preferences write an installation command to the clipboard; it is never read.
- Removing it: there is no uninstall button. Disabling the extension removes everything it adds to the shell and starts nothing more (the engine is a separate program, started by D-Bus on demand). To remove the engine, delete ~/.local/share/hold, ~/.local/share/voice-hold and the org.griffit.VoiceHold*.service files in ~/.local/share/dbus-1/services (or run `voice-hold-engine uninstall --models` if you installed the engine with pipx).
